newsitem.title: UK: Takeover panel pulls up Barings on Applied.
newsitem.headline: Takeover panel pulls up Barings on Applied.

text.p: Britain's takeover panel pulled up Barings Brothers International on Wednesday for breaching the code with respect to takeover offers received by one of its clients, Applied Distributors Group Plc
The takeover panel charged Barings for not consulting the panel before making an announcement with regard to the offers made for Applied.
The panel also said that the announcement should have been made earlier in view of the "substantial" rise in Applied Distribution's share price prior to the January 31 announcement.
In the announcement Applied had said that it had received a number of preliminary approaches involving indicative offers below the current market price of about 62 pence for its shares.
The announcement was made after its share price had shot up 15 pence to close at 61.5 on January 31, making it one of the top percentage gainers on the London bourse on that day.
"The executive has concluded that an earlier announcement should have been made," the panel said.
It said that but not consulting the panel, Barings had violated Rule 2.2 of the Code. "Barings was primarily responsible for these breaches of the code," it said.

Applied Distribution has issued a profit warning on November 7 saying it was "committed to maximising shareholder value" and was therefore "considering all options for the group's future development".
Its share price fell in the following week to 32.5 pence from 62.5 p.
The share price gathered strength in January and closed at 46.5p on January 30.
The panel pointed out that it should have been consulted after the share price moved more than 10 percent.
"In fact the executive was never consulted," it said.
